mainTopic: Going out on שבת with perfume containers, followed by אגדות about the luxury, immorality, and punishment of שומרון and ירושלים.
overview: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר disagree about a woman who goes out on שבת with a key, a כובלת, or a flask of פלייטון. It fixes a gap in the ברייתא and learns that an empty perfume flask makes her liable. רב אדא בר אהבה uses this to rule that carrying פחות מכשיעור of food in a vessel makes one liable, but רב אשי rejects the proof. Because perfume came up, the גמרא turns to the verses in עמוס about the luxuries of שומרון. It concludes that after the חורבן the רבנן banned only things that bring both pleasure and joy. Next, רבי אבהו explains the sin of the סְרֻחִים as wife-swapping, and three behaviors are listed that bring a person to poverty. The גמרא then explains the verses in ישעיה about the immodest בנות ציון and their punishments, each one matching the sin. It ends with רב's statement that the people of ירושלים were arrogant, and its example continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Which statement of רבי מאיר is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the referenced view of רבי מאיר is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the statement of רבי מאיר being referred to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי מאיר's opinion that was just mentioned. This is a setup line: the next step will quote that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the גמרא can analyze רבי מאיר's view, it needs the exact text where he says it. The question only points us toward a ברייתא; it does not challenge anything yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is it? (asks to identify something)
A תנא whose opinion is being identified

phrases.english: And what is the statement of Rabbi Meir?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by asking for the source of a view referenced just before.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the ברייתא that records רבי מאיר's opinion.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the key, the herb bundle, and the balsam flask
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted. רבי מאיר says a woman who goes out holding a key is חייב חטאת. רבי אליעזר exempts a כובלת and a צלוחית של פלייטון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: A woman may not go out with a key in her hand. If she went out, she must bring a חטאת. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי אליעזר exempts her when she goes out with a bundle of fragrant herbs or a flask of balsam oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting the ברייתא where רבי מאיר's view appears. רבי אליעזר's response is quoted with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats a key carried in the hand as real carrying, which brings a חטאת. רבי אליעזר disagrees about the perfume items: he does not obligate her for going out with them. Notice that רבי אליעזר names items that רבי מאיר never mentioned. The next step will attack exactly that point.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
She must bring a sin-offering (carried on שבת by accident)
A bundle or pouch of fragrant herbs or perfume
A small flask of balsam oil

phrases.english: As it was taught: A woman may not go out
with a key that is in her hand,
and if she went out, she is liable to bring a sin-offering;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Eliezer exempts
with a bundle of fragrant herbs and with a flask of balsam oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לֹא תֵּצֵא אִשָּׁה בְּמַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁבְּיָדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by quoting the source ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא: a woman going out with a key is חייב חטאת according to רבי מאיר; רבי אליעזר exempts the כובלת and the צלוחית של פלייטון.

steps.title: Who mentioned the herb bundle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: רבי אליעזר exempts a כובלת, but רבי מאיר never mentioned one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bundle of fragrant herbs — who mentioned it at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in the ברייתא. רבי אליעזר responds about items that no one had brought up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a dispute, the second opinion should answer the first. רבי מאיר spoke only about a key, so it makes no sense for רבי אליעזר to suddenly exempt perfume items. The text as written seems incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned its name? (this was never brought up)

phrases.english: A bundle of fragrant herbs — who mentioned its name?

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹבֶלֶת מַאן דְּכַר שְׁמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's exemption of the כובלת and the צלוחית in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר did not mention these items, so רבי אליעזר's response has nothing to respond to.

steps.title: The baraita is missing words, and the full text is restored
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is incomplete. The full version says רבי מאיר also obligates for the כובלת and the צלוחית, and רבי אליעזר exempts them only when they hold perfume.
steps.simpleTranslation: The text is missing words, and this is what it teaches: Likewise, she may not go out with a bundle of fragrant herbs or with a flask of balsam oil. If she went out, she must bring a חטאת. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי אליעזר exempts the bundle of herbs and the flask of balsam oil. When is this said? When there is perfume in them. But if there is no perfume in them, she is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by adding the missing words. With them, רבי מאיר does mention the perfume items, and רבי אליעזר's exemption has a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing line restored, רבי מאיר obligates a חטאת for the perfume items as well, so רבי אליעזר is now answering something real. The restored text also adds a condition: רבי אליעזר exempts only when perfume is inside. With perfume inside, the container is worn the way a woman wears jewelry. When it is empty, it is just a container, and even רבי אליעזר holds her liable.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches
In what case is this said? (introduces a limit)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is changing the law because it dislikes it. חסורי מחסרא means the original wording was shortened, and the גמרא is restoring the full meaning. The added condition (only with perfume inside) is part of רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between a container with perfume and an empty one is exactly what רב אדא בר אהבה builds on in the next step.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
And likewise with a bundle of fragrant herbs

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בִּצְלוֹחִית שֶׁל פִּלְיָיטוֹן לֹא תֵּצֵא,
phrases.english: and likewise with a flask of balsam oil, she may not go out,
and if she went out, she is liable to bring a sin-offering;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Eliezer exempts with a bundle of fragrant herbs
and with a flask of balsam oil.
In what case are these words said?
When there is perfume in them;
but if there is no perfume in them, she is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מִחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by restoring the missing text of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as written has רבי מאיר discussing only a key, so רבי אליעזר's mention of the כובלת seems out of place.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר also obligates for the כובלת and the צלוחית. רבי אליעזר exempts only when perfume is inside; an empty one makes her liable.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: carrying less than the minimum amount of food in a vessel makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה learns from the ברייתא that someone who carries פחות מכשיעור of food inside a vessel is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: This teaches that someone who carries out less than the minimum amount of food inside a vessel is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא draws a new הלכה from the restored ברייתא. He states his conclusion first; the next step shows how he gets it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when you carry food in a container, the container is secondary to the food, and you are not liable for it separately. But if the food is less than the minimum amount, the food does not count, so the vessel is no longer secondary to anything. You become liable for carrying the vessel itself.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches (a new rule drawn from a source)
One who carries out (from one domain to another)
Less than the minimum amount that makes one liable

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
This is to say
one who carries out food less than the minimum measure
in a vessel is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new הלכה from the restored ברייתא's ruling about an empty container.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who carries פחות מכשיעור of food inside a vessel is חייב, because of the vessel.

steps.title: Why the empty perfume flask proves the rule
steps.stepSummary: An empty perfume container that still has a scent is like a vessel holding less than the minimum amount, and the ברייתא says she is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a container with no perfume in it is like a vessel holding less than the minimum amount, and the ברייתא teaches that she is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה explains his proof. He compares the empty perfume flask to a vessel holding a tiny amount of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'empty' perfume flask still holds a trace of scent, which is like having less than the minimum amount inside. Since the ברייתא says she is liable for it, the small leftover does not protect the container. In the same way, a vessel holding less than the minimum amount of food makes the carrier liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Is similar to, is comparable to

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא was missing words. רבי מאיר obligates a חטאת for the perfume items too. רבי אליעזר exempts them only when perfume is inside. Because an empty container brings liability, רב אדא בר אהבה rules that carrying פחות מכשיעור of food in a vessel makes one liable for the vessel.

phrases.english: For behold, one with no perfume in it
is comparable to less than the measure in a vessel,
and it teaches that she is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא אֵין בָּהּ בּוֹשֶׂם כְּפָחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר בִּכְלִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that carrying פחות מכשיעור of food in a vessel brings liability.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The restored ברייתא: an empty perfume container (a scent with no real perfume) makes her liable.

steps.title: An empty perfume flask is different from a vessel with a little food
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects רב אדא בר אהבה's proof. Normally, carrying less than a שיעור inside a vessel may be פטור. The empty perfume flask is different because there is no substance in it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: In general, I would tell you he is exempt. But here it is different, because there is no real substance in the flask at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that the ברייתא about the empty perfume flask does not prove רב אדא בר אהבה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a vessel holds some food, even less than a שיעור, the person is carrying the food and the vessel is secondary to it. So he can be פטור. A perfume flask with only a smell holds nothing real, so the flask itself is what is being carried, and that makes her חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from punishment or a חטאת

steps.whatToRemember: The question of carrying less than a שיעור inside a vessel stays open. רב אשי says an empty flask with only a scent is not the same case, because a scent is not 'something'.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In רב אשי's view, a vessel with a little food may be פטור, but a totally empty vessel (even one that smells) is חייב. The empty one is more liable because nothing inside it takes away the vessel's importance.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
In general, I would tell you he is exempt,
phrases.notes: For example, a vessel with less than a שיעור of food

phrases.english: but here it is different,
phrases.notes: The case of the empty perfume flask

phrases.english: since there is no substance at all.
phrases.notes: Only a scent remains, so the flask itself is what is carried

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּעָלְמָא אֵימָא לָךְ פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not decide רב אדא בר אהבה's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison fails. A scent is not 'less than a שיעור' of substance. It is no substance at all, so the empty flask cannot teach about a vessel holding a small amount of food.

steps.title: The 'chief oils' in the verse are balsam oil
steps.stepSummary: Since perfume came up, the גמרא quotes a verse from עמוס. רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, identifies its 'chief oils' as פלייטון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And they anoint themselves with the chief oils.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: this is balsam oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new side topic connected to perfume. It explains which oil the verse in עמוס means, and this sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in עמוס criticizes people who live in luxury and do not feel the pain of the people's destruction. By naming the oil as פלייטון, שמואל suggests that using it is the kind of indulgence the נביא criticizes.

phrases.english: "And anoint themselves with the chief oils,"
phrases.notes: עמוס ו:ו

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
this is balsam oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵאשִׁית שְׁמָנִים יִמְשָׁחוּ, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected only by the shared subject of perfume and פלייטון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'chief oils' the נביא criticizes are פלייטון.

steps.title: The חכמים rejected a decree against balsam oil
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects. רבי יהודה בן בבא decreed against פלייטון, and the חכמים did not agree with him. If the verse condemns it as a pleasure, why did they disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: רבי יהודה בן בבא decreed even against balsam oil, and the sages did not agree with him. If you say the verse condemns it because it is a pleasure, why did they not agree with him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges שמואל's identification, using a source where the חכמים refused to ban פלייטון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בבא wanted to ban פלייטון as a sign of mourning for the חורבן. If the verse really condemns פלייטון as a luxury, the decree seems fully justified. The fact that the חכמים rejected it suggests that פלייטון is not what the verse means.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
They did not agree with him

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּלְיָיטוֹן גְּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא,
phrases.english: Even on balsam oil Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava made a decree,
phrases.notes: A ban as mourning for the חורבן

phrases.english: and they did not agree with him.
And if you say it is because of pleasure,
phrases.notes: That the verse condemns פלייטון as a luxury

phrases.english: why did they not agree with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב יוֹסֵף: אַף עַל פִּלְיָיטוֹן גְּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's identification from Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the 'chief oils' are פלייטון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the נביא condemns פלייטון as a luxury, a decree banning it should have been accepted. The חכמים rejected it, so the identification looks wrong.

steps.title: By that logic, the wine vessels in the same verse would be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רב יוסף with a counter-question. The same verse criticizes drinking wine from מזרקי יין. Would that be forbidden as well?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: According to your reasoning, the verse also says 'who drink wine in מזרקי יין.' רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree about this. One says these are multi-spouted vessels. The other says they throw their cups to one another. Is that also forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends שמואל by turning רב יוסף's logic against him, using the other half of the very same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that whatever the verse criticizes must be banned. אביי points out that the verse also criticizes drinking from fancy wine vessels, and no one bans that. So the verse being critical does not automatically create a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (a counter-argument)
Wine vessels mentioned in the verse

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי and רבי אסי are only explaining a word. Their disagreement is not the main point. What matters is אביי's question: is drinking this way forbidden?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And according to your reasoning,
that which is written: "who drink wine in mizrekei"
phrases.notes: The same verse in עמוס

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi disagree:
one said: multi-spouted vessels,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר שֶׁמְּזָרְקִין כּוֹסוֹתֵיהֶן זֶה לָזֶה.
phrases.english: and one said: they throw their cups to one another.
Is that also forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 9 with a counter-question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything the verse condemns as luxury must be formally banned, so rejecting the פלייטון decree disproves שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse criticizes things that are clearly not banned, so a rejected decree does not disprove שמואל's identification.

steps.title: A sage saw the ריש גלותא drink from such a vessel and said nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves that drinking from קנישקנין is permitted. רבה בר רב הונא saw the ריש גלותא drink from one and did not object.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבה בר רב הונא visited the house of the ריש גלותא, and the ריש גלותא drank from a multi-spouted vessel, and רבה בר רב הונא said nothing at all to him!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his counter-question with a real event, showing that these wine vessels were used freely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If drinking from קנישקנין were forbidden, a sage like רבה בר רב הונא would have protested. His silence shows it is allowed, even though the verse criticizes it. That supports אביי's point that the verse alone does not create a ban.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of Babylonian Jewry

steps.whatToRemember: The verse in עמוס criticizes luxury, but that alone does not make every item it mentions forbidden. This is how אביי protects שמואל's identification of פלייטון from רב יוסף's challenge.

phrases.english: But Rabba bar Rav Huna
visited the house of the Exilarch
and he (the Exilarch) drank from a multi-spouted vessel,
and he said nothing at all to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the counter-question of Step 10 with an event
steps.raayaObject: Drinking from קנישקנין, mentioned critically in the verse, is not forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story: רבה בר רב הונא saw the ריש גלותא drink from קנישקנין and did not object.

steps.title: The rule: pleasure with joy was banned, pleasure alone was not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the רבנן banned only things that have both תענוג and שמחה. Something with תענוג but no שמחה, like פלייטון, was not banned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: anything that has pleasure and also has joy, the רבנן made a decree against. But anything that has pleasure and has no joy, the רבנן did not make a decree against.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up רב יוסף's question with a clear rule. This explains why the חכמים did not agree with רבי יהודה בן בבא's ban on פלייטון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף asked: if the verse condemns פלייטון, why didn't the חכמים ban it? The answer is that a verse criticizing a luxury does not automatically make it forbidden. In mourning for the חורבן, the רבנן banned only joyful celebration, such as wine with music. Plain physical pleasure, like perfumed oil, was not banned.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis made a decree (a rabbinic ban)

steps.whatToRemember: After the חורבן, the רבנן banned things that are pleasure plus joy. Pleasure alone, like פלייטון, was not banned.
steps.confusionAlert: The verse in עמוס does criticize פלייטון as part of a spoiled lifestyle. But being criticized is not the same as being forbidden. The ban depends only on whether the thing brings שמחה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains which luxuries were limited as mourning for the בית המקדש. It answers רב יוסף's question from Step 9.

phrases.english: Rather: any matter
phrases.notes: Introduces the final rule

phrases.english: that has pleasure in it
and has joy in it
the Rabbis decreed against it
phrases.notes: As mourning for the חורבן

phrases.english: but a matter that has pleasure in it
and has no joy in it
phrases.notes: Like פלייטון

phrases.english: the Rabbis did not decree against it

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כׇּל מִידֵּי דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תַּעֲנוּג וְאִית בֵּיהּ שִׂמְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the wine example from Steps 10-11 into a general rule that answers רב יוסף's question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Things with both pleasure and joy were banned after the חורבן. Things with pleasure but no joy, like פלייטון, were not.

steps.title: A first reading of 'stretched out on their couches'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another verse from the same passage in עמוס. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads 'וּסְרֻחִים' as describing a disgusting habit: urinating naked in front of their beds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Those who lie on beds of ivory and stretch out on their couches.' רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: This teaches that they would urinate in front of their beds while naked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining the verses in עמוס about the spoiled people of שומרון. Here it moves to the word 'וּסְרֻחִים'. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gives the first explanation of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סְרֻחִים sounds like סִרְחוֹן, 'a bad smell'. So רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads it as a disgusting, smelly habit. On his reading, the sin is crude behavior, not a serious עבירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Beds of ivory (a sign of luxury)
Stretched out; read here as connected to a bad smell
It teaches (introduces a lesson drawn from a verse)

phrases.english: "Those who lie upon beds of ivory
phrases.notes: עמוס ו:ד

phrases.english: and stretch out upon their couches"
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
This teaches that they would urinate
in front of their beds while naked.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשֹּׁכְבִים עַל מִטּוֹת שֵׁן וּסְרֻחִים עַל עַרְשׂוֹתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the same passage in עמוס that Step 8 began explaining, and now explains a different phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סְרֻחִים refers to a crude habit: urinating naked in front of their beds.

steps.title: Exile is too harsh a punishment for that
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו mocks רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reading. A later verse says these people will be exiled first. That makes no sense for something as small as a crude habit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו mocked this: If so, is this what is written: 'Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of the exiles'? Because they urinate in front of their beds naked, they will be exiled at the head of the exiles?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו attacks the reading from Step 13. He uses a later verse in the same passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמוס ו:ז says these same סְרֻחִים will be the first to go into exile. That is an extremely severe punishment. A crude but minor habit cannot be the reason for it, so the word must describe a much worse sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this what is written? (here, said with surprise)
They will go into exile at the head of the exiles

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu ridiculed it:
If so, is this what is written:
"Therefore now they shall go into exile at the head of the exiles"
phrases.notes: עמוס ו:ז

phrases.english: because they urinate
in front of their beds while naked
they will be exiled at the head of the exiles?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: that punishment is far too severe

steps.triggerLanguage: מְגַדֵּף בַּהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's explanation that סְרֻחִים means urinating naked in front of their beds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The punishment and the sin must match. Being exiled first is too heavy a punishment for a minor crude habit.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's reading: shameful immoral behavior
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that סְרֻחִים describes people who feasted together, pushed their beds together, and swapped wives. A sin this serious fits the punishment of exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבהו said: These are people who would eat and drink with each other, push their beds together, swap their wives with each other, and make their couches foul with seed that was not their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו drops the first reading and gives his own explanation of סְרֻחִים. It describes a grave sin that fits the punishment of exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו still reads סְרֻחִים as 'making foul'. But for him the foulness comes from עריות, forbidden relations, which are among the most serious sins. That explains why these people deserve to be the first ones exiled.

keyTerms.meaning: Made foul, made smell (connected to סְרֻחִים)

steps.whatToRemember: The punishment in the verse decides the meaning. Because the exile is so severe, סְרֻחִים must describe the grave sin of עריות, not a minor crude habit.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abahu said:
These are people who would
eat and drink with each other,
and push their beds against each other,
and swap their wives with each other,
and make their couches foul
phrases.notes: A play on the word סְרֻחִים

phrases.english: with seed that was not their own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that was rejected in Step 14 with a new one that fits the punishment.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reading of the verse in place of the rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סְרֻחִים describes a minor crude habit of urinating naked in front of their beds.
steps.terutzMaskana: סְרֻחִים describes wife-swapping and forbidden relations, a sin serious enough to earn the punishment of exile.

steps.title: Three things that bring a person to poverty
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, or a ברייתא, teaches that three behaviors lead to poverty: urinating naked in front of one's bed, being careless with נטילת ידים, and having one's wife curse him to his face.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said, and some say a ברייתא taught: Three things bring a person to poverty. They are: one who urinates naked in front of his bed, one who is careless about washing his hands, and one whose wife curses him to his face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that lists three behaviors that cause a person to become poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching is linked to the previous discussion. The first item, urinating naked in front of one's bed, is the exact habit רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא found in the word סְרֻחִים. רבי אבהו said that habit was too minor to earn exile, but here we learn it still carries a real consequence: poverty. The next lines of the גמרא will explain each item one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
The ritual washing of the hands

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: There are two versions of who said this teaching.

phrases.english: Three things bring a person
to poverty, and these are they:
one who urinates in front of his bed while naked,
and one who is careless about washing his hands,
and one whose wife curses him to his face.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This opens a related topic. It picks up the habit of urinating naked in front of one's bed from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reading in step 13 and lists it among three causes of poverty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three behaviors bring poverty: urinating naked in front of one's bed, being careless with נטילת ידים, and a wife cursing her husband to his face.

steps.title: Only when facing the bed
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the first item. It applies only when the person faces his bed while urinating. Facing away, toward the outside of the room, is not a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: About one who urinates naked in front of his bed, רבא said: We only said this when he turns his face toward his bed. If he faces outward, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the first item on the list and makes it narrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in front of his bed' could describe anyone urinating near his bed. רבא says the problem is only when the person faces the bed and urinates toward it. That is what makes it disgusting. If he turns toward the outer part of the room, the teaching does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in the case of, a formula that limits a teaching
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: One who urinates in front of his bed while naked:
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the first item again so it can explain it.

phrases.english: Rava said: We only said this
when he turns his face toward his bed,
but if he faces outward, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains and narrows the first of the three items from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern applies only when the person faces his bed. Facing outward is not a problem.

steps.title: Only onto the floor, not into a container
steps.stepSummary: Even when he faces the bed, the teaching applies only if he urinates onto the floor. Urinating into a container is not a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when he faces his bed, we only said this when he urinates onto the ground. If he urinates into a container, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the first item a second time, inside the case רבא just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two conditions: he must face the bed, and he must urinate onto the floor. Using a container takes away the disgusting part, so the teaching no longer applies. The rule keeps getting smaller until only the truly crude case is left.

phrases.english: And when he turns his face toward his bed,
too, we only said this when he urinates onto the ground,
but into a container, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ לְפוּרְיֵיהּ, נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְאַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This adds a second limit inside the case described in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when facing the bed, the concern applies only to urinating onto the floor, not into a container.

steps.title: Careless hand-washing means not washing at all
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that being careless with נטילת ידים means not washing at all. Washing with only a small amount of water is not a problem here.
steps.simpleTranslation: About one who is careless about washing his hands, רבא said: We only said this when he does not wash his hands at all. If he washes, but not in the full proper way, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains and narrows the second item on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Careless' could mean many things. רבא says the punishment of poverty is only for someone who skips washing completely. Someone who washes, even with less water than ideal, does not fall under this teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: He washed, but not properly, for example with too little water

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase מְשָׁא וְלָא מְשָׁא does not mean 'he washed and he didn't wash' as if that were a contradiction. It means he did wash, just not fully or with enough water.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא narrows each item so it covers only the truly bad case. Urinating counts only when facing the bed and onto the floor. For washing, רבא limits it to not washing at all, but the very next step (Step 20) rejects that limit: washing with only a little water also falls short.

phrases.english: And one who is careless about washing his hands:
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the second item so it can explain it.

phrases.english: Rava said: We only said this
when he does not wash his hands at all,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְשָׁא וְלָא מְשָׁא — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if he washes, just not properly, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְזַלְזֵל בִּנְטִילַת יָדַיִם, אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the first item, the גמרא returns to the list from step 16 and explains the second item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being careless with נטילת ידים refers only to not washing at all. Washing with too little water is not included.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that a little water is enough for washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea from Step 19 that washing with a small amount of water avoids the problem. רב חסדא washed with handfuls of water and was rewarded with handfuls of goodness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is not correct, because רב חסדא said: I wash with full handfuls of water, and they gave me full handfuls of goodness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on what was just said in Step 19, that washing with a little water is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the poverty warning only applies to someone who does not wash at all. Here the גמרא says that is not right: רב חסדא's experience shows that using plenty of water brings blessing. So washing with only a little water is also missing something.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is not so; a phrase that rejects the previous statement

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not reject the whole idea of נטילת ידים bringing blessing. It only rejects the claim that a small amount of water is good enough.

phrases.english: And that is not so,
phrases.notes: This pushes back on the limit set in Step 19.

phrases.english: for Rav Ḥisda said:
I wash with full handfuls of water
and they gave me full handfuls of goodness.
phrases.notes: Measure for measure: plenty of water, plenty of blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו מִלְּתָא הִיא, דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second half of Step 19 (that a little water is fine).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that washing with a small amount of water avoids the problem.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב חסדא's testimony shows that using a lot of water is what brings blessing, so a small amount falls short.

steps.title: What kind of cursing by a wife brings poverty
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the third item: the wife curses her husband over her jewelry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about the case of 'his wife curses him to his face', רבא said: this is about her jewelry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the third cause of poverty from Step 16, a wife who curses her husband to his face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא narrows the case. It is not about any curse at all. It is about a wife who is upset that her husband does not provide her with jewelry.

keyTerms.meaning: She curses him to his face

phrases.english: And regarding one whose wife curses him to his face,
phrases.notes: Quotes the third item from Step 16.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is about matters of her jewelry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁאִשְׁתּוֹ מְקַלַּלְתּוֹ בְּפָנָיו, אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second item (washing) to the third item (the wife's curse).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The curse that brings poverty is one about her jewelry.

steps.title: Only when he can afford the jewelry but does not buy it
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only when the husband has the means and still does not provide jewelry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only when he has the money and does not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a further limit to רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband is poor and cannot afford jewelry, her curse does not bring poverty on him. The problem is a husband who could give but chooses not to.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only... (introduces a limit)

steps.whatToRemember: All three causes of poverty have now been narrowed: facing the bed and urinating on the floor, not washing properly, and a wife's justified complaint about jewelry he could afford.

phrases.english: And this applies only
when he has the means and does not do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי הוּא דְּאִית לֵיהּ וְלָא עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's explanation in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife's curse about jewelry brings poverty only if the husband can afford it and refuses.

steps.title: The immodest walking of the daughters of Zion
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרב עילאי explains the פסוק in ישעיה about the haughty בנות ציון, phrase by phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא son of רב עילאי taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'Because the daughters of Zion are haughty'? They walked with a tall, upright posture. 'And walk with outstretched necks': they walked heel next to toe. 'And wanton eyes': they filled their eyes with blue eye shadow and winked. 'Walking and mincing': a tall woman walked next to a short one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. Since it spoke about the sins of the first בית המקדש era (Step 15), it now explains another פסוק about that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק is read as a specific way the women drew attention to themselves. They walked tall, took tiny showy steps, used eye makeup and winked, and paired a tall woman with a short one so the tall one would stand out.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughters of Zion (women of ירושלים)
Heel next to big toe (tiny steps)

phrases.english: Rava son of Rav Ilai expounded:
What is that which is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ יַעַן כִּי גָבְהוּ בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן״ —
phrases.english: “The Lord said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty” —
phrases.notes: ישעיה 3:16.

phrases.english: that they would walk with an upright stature.
“And they walk with outstretched necks” —
that they would walk heel beside toe.
phrases.notes: Tiny steps so people would notice them.

phrases.english: “And wanton eyes” —
that they would fill their eyes with eye shadow
and wink.
phrases.notes: Signaling to men with their eyes.

phrases.english: “Walking and mincing” —
that they would walk a tall woman beside a short one.
phrases.notes: So the tall woman would stand out.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עִילָּאֵי, מַאי דִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of poverty and starts a new אגדה about sins of the first בית המקדש era.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes specific immodest, attention-seeking behaviors of the בנות ציון.

steps.title: Perfume in their shoes to tempt the young men
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק explains 'making a tinkling with their feet': the women put perfume in their shoes and splashed it at young men.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And with their feet they make a tinkling': רב יצחק of the school of רבי אמי said: This teaches that they put myrrh and balsam in their shoes and walked in the markets of ירושלים. When they got near the young men of Israel, they stamped on the ground, sprayed the perfume at them, and put the יצר הרע into them like the poison of a snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining the same פסוק. Now it explains the last phrase, about their feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The women hid perfume in their shoes. By stamping their feet near young men, they released the scent on purpose to stir up desire. The גמרא compares it to a snake's poison: small, but it spreads through the whole body.

keyTerms.meaning: They make a tinkling (with their feet)
Like the venom of a viper

phrases.english: “And with their feet they make a tinkling” —

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak of the school of Rabbi Ami said:
This teaches that they would put myrrh and balsam in their shoes
and walk in the marketplaces of Jerusalem,
and once they reached the young men of Israel
they would stamp on the ground and splash it at them
and put the evil inclination into them
like the venom of a viper.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְרַגְלֵיהֶן תְּעַכַּסְנָה — אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the same פסוק, with a different speaker for its last phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Tinkling with their feet' means releasing hidden perfume to tempt young men.

steps.title: What was their punishment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what punishment came for these sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was their punishment?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא asks about the punishment, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After listing the sins, the גמרא wants to know how they were punished. The answer will show that each punishment matched the sin.

phrases.english: What was their punishment?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי פּוּרְעֲנוּתַיְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sins to their punishment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What punishment matched the sins of the בנות ציון.

steps.title: Each punishment matched the sin
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא explains a later פסוק: every body part they used to show off was struck with a matching punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר עולא taught: 'Instead of a sweet smell there will be rot': the place they perfumed became rotting sores. 'Instead of a sash, a rope (נקפה)': the place they tied with a sash became full of bruises. 'Instead of styled hair, baldness': the place they adorned became bald patches. 'Instead of a fine dress (פתיגיל), sackcloth': the openings that lead to pleasure became places for sackcloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 25 using רבה בר עולא's explanation of ישעיה 3:24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is 'measure for measure'. Each spot they used for sin, such as perfume, a sash, or styled hair, became the spot of their punishment. Some explanations are based on wordplay: נקפה becomes נקפים (bruises), and פתיגיל is read as פתחים plus גילה (openings plus pleasure).

keyTerms.meaning: Fine dress; read here as פתחים + גילה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common theme in חז״ל: punishment is מדה כנגד מדה, matching the exact way the sin was done.

phrases.english: As Rabba bar Ulla expounded:
“And instead of a sweet smell there shall be rot” —
phrases.notes: ישעיה 3:24.

phrases.english: the place where they would perfume themselves
became full of rotting sores.
“And instead of a sash, a rope” —
the place where they were girded with a sash
became full of bruises.
phrases.notes: Wordplay: נקפה becomes נקפים.

phrases.english: “And instead of well-set hair, baldness” —
the place where they would adorn themselves
became full of bald patches.
“And instead of a fine dress, a girding of sackcloth” —
the openings that lead to pleasure
phrases.notes: The word פתיגיל is read as פתחים plus גיל.

phrases.english: will become a place for a girding of sackcloth.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְדָרֵישׁ רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their punishments struck the very body parts they used to show off: rot, bruises, baldness, and sackcloth.

steps.title: Instead of beauty, a sore
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the last phrase of the פסוק with a popular saying: instead of beauty comes a sore.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For instead of beauty': רבא said, this is what people say: in exchange for beauty, a sore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פסוק by explaining its last words, with a common saying quoted by רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כי in the פסוק is linked to the Aramaic כיבא, meaning a sore or wound. So the beauty they showed off was replaced by an ugly wound, as people commonly say.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a popular saying)

steps.whatToRemember: The בנות ציון used their beauty and their bodies to tempt people, and each part they used for this was punished in a matching way: מדה כנגד מדה.

phrases.english: “A brand instead of beauty” —
Rava said:
This is what people say:
In exchange for beauty — a sore.
phrases.notes: כי is read as כיבא, a sore.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תַחַת יֹפִי — אָמַר רָבָא, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the punishment פסוק with its final phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beauty used for sin is replaced by a sore.

steps.title: The scab on the daughters of Zion was leprosy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that the word וְסִפַּח in the פסוק means the בנות ציון were struck with צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion.' רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: this teaches that צרעת broke out on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining the punishment פסוקים from ישעיה. Here רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains the word וְסִפַּח: the punishment was צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבה בר עולא showed that each body part they showed off was punished. Now one specific punishment is named: the 'scab' on their heads was a real case of צרעת. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And He will strike with a scab (from the פסוק in ישעיה)
A spiritual skin disease, often translated as 'leprosy'

phrases.english: "And the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion"
phrases.notes: ישעיה ג:יז

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
This teaches that leprosy broke out among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the punishment פסוקים after רבא's explanation in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וְסִפַּח in the פסוק means the בנות ציון were struck with צרעת.

steps.title: Proof from a matching word in the laws of leprosy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא proves his reading: the same root (ספח) shows up in ויקרא in the list of צרעת marks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is written 'וְשִׂפַּח', and there (in the laws of צרעת) it is written 'for a שְׂאֵת and for a סַפַּחַת.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for the previous step. The same word-root appears in the תורה's list of צרעת types, so it must mean צרעת here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא יד:נו, סַפַּחַת is one of the official kinds of צרעת marks. Since ישעיה uses the same root, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads it with the same meaning. This is a simple word-match, 'here' and 'there'.

keyTerms.meaning: A raised swelling, one type of צרעת mark
A scab, another type of צרעת mark

steps.confusionAlert: The text spells the word וְסִפַּח with a ס in the quote and וְשִׂפַּח with a שׂ in the proof. It is the same word from the פסוק, and both sounds point to the same root as סַפַּחַת.

phrases.english: It is written here: "ve-sippach" [scab],
and it is written there: "For a sore, and for a scab [sappachat]."
phrases.notes: ויקרא יד:נו, in the laws of צרעת

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא ״וְשִׂפַּח״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 28's claim that the scab was צרעת.
steps.raayaObject: That וְסִפַּח in ישעיה means צרעת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא יד:נו, which lists סַפַּחַת as a type of צרעת.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about 'their openings'
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל give two different explanations of the phrase פתהן יערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the Lord will lay bare their secret parts.' רב and שמואל disagree. One says: their insides poured out like a jug. The other says: their openings became like a forest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the same פסוק. רב and שמואל each read the hard word יְעָרֶה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One reads יְעָרֶה as 'pour out', like emptying a jug, so their insides spilled out. The other reads it as יַעַר, 'forest', so their private openings grew thick hair like a forest. Both fit the idea of a punishment that matches their sin of showing off their bodies.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say which opinion belongs to רב and which to שמואל. It just says 'one says… and one says'.

phrases.english: "And the Lord will lay bare their secret parts."
phrases.notes: End of ישעיה ג:יז

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree:
One says: that they [their insides] were poured out like a jug,
phrases.notes: Reads יְעָרֶה as 'pour out'

phrases.english: and one says: that their openings became [overgrown with hair] like a forest.
phrases.notes: Reads יְעָרֶה like יַעַר

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the פסוק (וְסִפַּח) to its second half (פתהן יערה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two readings of פתהן יערה: their insides poured out like a jug, or their openings became like a forest.
steps.whatToRemember: The punishment of the בנות ציון matched their sin: the same body they used to show off was struck, with צרעת on the head and shame in their private parts.

steps.title: The people of Jerusalem were arrogant
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the people of ירושלים were insolent, arrogant people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the people of ירושלים were people of arrogance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the women of ציון to a general statement about the sins of the people of ירושלים. This line sets up the examples that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was the pride of the בנות ציון. Now רב widens it: the whole city had a culture of שחץ, a bold, shameless arrogance. The next step will show what that looked like in their everyday talk.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The people of Jerusalem were people of arrogance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic: from the punishment of the בנות ציון to the general arrogance of ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of ירושלים were אנשי שחץ, arrogant and shameless.

steps.title: An example of their coded dinner talk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show רב's example: people asked each other about their 'meal' in code words that really referred to immoral behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person would say to his friend: 'What did you dine on today? Well-kneaded bread, or bread that is not well-kneaded? White wine, or…'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the example that proves step 31. This passage stops in the middle of the sentence, so the example continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface they are talking about bread and wine. On the next amud, רב חסדא says all of these were code words for immoral relationships (וכולן לזנות), and they bragged about it openly. That bold, shameless talk is the שחץ that רב was describing.

keyTerms.meaning: Well-kneaded bread (used here as a code word)
White wine (used here as a code word)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as a real question about food. The food words are a cover for crude, immoral talk, and that is exactly why the גמרא brings it as proof of their arrogance.

phrases.english: A person would say to his friend:
On what did you dine today?

phrases.aramaic: בְּפַת עֲמִילָה, אוֹ בְּפַת שֶׁאֵינָהּ עֲמִילָה?
phrases.english: On well-kneaded bread, or on bread that is not well-kneaded?
phrases.notes: A hidden reference to immoral relationships, as רב חסדא says on the next amud (וכולן לזנות)

phrases.english: On white wine, or…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם אוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ: בַּמֶּה סָעַדְתָּ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what the arrogance described in step 31 looked like in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of ירושלים openly bragged about immoral acts using coded 'meal' language.
